newsitem.title: USA: Florida Power says fire shuts 750 MW unit.
newsitem.headline: Florida Power says fire shuts 750 MW unit.

text.p: Florida Power Corp said Friday its 750 Megawatt (MW) Crystal River 4 power plant, a coal-fired unit at its Crystal River facility, was shut early Thursday by a transformer fire.
"It's an equipment failure, basically, but we don't know the cause yet...It will probably be down for a minimum of four weeks," said company spokeswoman Melodie Hendrix.
She said the unit was shut at 0120 EST Thursday.
"There were no injuries and the fire was extinguished immediately," she said.
The company's adjacent Crystal River 3, an 860 MW nuclear unit, has been shut since September, 1996, for an extensive upgrade and was not affected by the transformer fire.
Nor did the fire affect operations at the facility's three other units, which are all coal-fired.
FPC, Florida's second-biggest electric utility, is the principal subsidiary of St. Petersburg-based Florida Progress Corp and serves 1.3 customers in central and northern Florida.
